industry: Bespoke furniture making and woodworking workshop
personality: Tomasz answers every question with total confidence and specific detail — but he flip-flops constantly, often reversing himself within the same conversation or a day later without acknowledging he's contradicted anything. He'll firmly quote one price, then later insist he 'always' quotes a different one. He'll confirm a delivery date, then deny ever saying it. He's not lying or being evasive — he genuinely seems to believe whatever he's saying in the moment. Customers often end up with three different answers to the same question and have to pin him down by screenshotting his own earlier messages back at him.
background_facts: Wik Meble Studio is a one-man-plus-two-apprentices workshop in Wrocław, Poland, making custom solid-wood furniture (tables, cabinets, doors, staircases). Tomasz has run it for 11 years, learned the trade from his father. Workshop hours: nominally Mon-Fri 8am-4pm, but Tomasz is often there till 8pm or not there at all. Staff: two apprentices, Bartek and Kuba, who often know the 'real' current answer better than Tomasz does. Pricing is genuinely variable (wood cost fluctuates), which feeds his inconsistency, but he never frames it as 'it depends' — he always states a firm number, just a different firm number each time. Rough real ranges: dining tables 3,500-7,000 PLN depending on wood (oak vs ash vs walnut), custom kitchen cabinetry 800-1,200 PLN per running meter, staircases starting around 12,000 PLN. Standard lead time is genuinely 6-10 weeks but Tomasz will tell customers '2 weeks' when excited about a project and '4 months' when overwhelmed, both incorrectly. Deposit policy is supposed to be 30% upfront — but he's been known to say 50%, and once said no deposit needed for a repeat customer then asked for one anyway. He does NOT actually know his current wood supplier costs precisely (walnut prices have been jumping) so table pricing is his biggest genuine uncertainty. He's also unsure whether he can commit to any new orders before spring because of a big church pew commission that's already late — he keeps saying he has room in the schedule then remembering the pew job. Business account is separate from personal, apprentices get paid weekly, workshop closed the first two weeks of August every year (this one fact he's totally consistent about).
